title: Hybrid radiomics and deep-learning model stratifies risk in O-RADS 4 adnexal masses
summary: A model combining ultrasound radiomics, a transfer-learning CNN score and clinical predictors was developed on 653 retrospective patients from four centers (132 in external validation) and tested in a prospective cohort of 126. AUCs were 0.88 (95% CI 0.82-0.93) prospectively and 0.86 (0.78-0.92) externally, with pathology as the reference. In the prospective set six radiologists read cases with and without model assistance, and assistance improved accuracy and specificity across all readers.
ai_technology: Radiomics machine-learning classifiers plus a transfer-learning convolutional neural network combined with clinical predictors
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: Performance was assessed in external (n = 132) and prospective (n = 126) cohorts, with a six-reader assistance comparison.
evidence.unknown: Reader-assist figures are truncated in the abstract; effect on patient outcomes is not tested. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML radiomics and CNN scores were merged into a hybrid classifier of benign versus borderline or malignant masses.
